dedupe_keys.name: an agent based model to identify management practices integrity and performance in kenya s and ghana s water service delivery

description: Francesc Bellaubi, Georg Holtz and Claudia Pahl-Wostl published this agent-based model of water-service delivery. It draws on empirical research by Transparency International Kenya and Ghana Integrity Initiative. Principal-agent games represent social dilemmas, with payoffs based on transparency, accountability, participation and social costs. Bounded-rational actors consider expected payoffs and social comparisons when choosing management practices. Coverage is the documented Kenya and Ghana research context; geographic resolution, simulation time steps and a transferable validation dataset are not stated in the inspected metadata. It supports agent-based comparison of water-service governance arrangements. It models institutional behaviour and does not establish pipe-network hydraulic performance. Release 1.3.0 is available free through the CoMSES code repository and lists NetLogo. The release licence is CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0. Source code and model data were not downloaded or executed. Related resources include the CoMSES computational model library.
